## Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. It changed in two distinct ways.

In May 2000, at President Bill Clinton’s direction, the United States stopped using the feature to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide. In September 2007, the government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability.

The 2007 announcement was not the operational switch-off. It specified the feature’s omission from a future generation, extending the 2000 policy to GPS III.
